tasks.short: Write and check the specifications behind our HR dashboards and reports.

today.trigger: A new HR report is requested, a metric changes, or an AFAS extract or Power BI model needs updating.
steps: Clarify the question, audience and metric definitions with the HR requester.
Inspect available fields, joins and refresh timing in the AFAS extract and Power BI model.
Check whether Recruitee or Studytube exports are needed and how records can be linked.
Write source mappings, calculation rules, access requirements and acceptance examples in SharePoint.
Review the specification against the implementation and resolve differences with the requester.
systems: AFAS Profit and its nightly reporting extract
Recruitee and Studytube exports where available
drudgery: Copying field names, formulas and relationships into documents
Rewriting similar specifications for different sites
Comparing documentation with the latest report version
today.time_sinks: Reconstructing undocumented calculations and resolving definitions such as whether flex workers count in headcount or which hires have reached day 90.

lenses.faster: Extract model metadata and generate source tables, calculation descriptions and change comparisons automatically. I review disputed definitions and failed checks instead of copying technical details.
lenses.autonomous: A changed model export or approved reporting request starts a draft specification and validation run. Publication waits for my approval.
lenses.ambitious: Document every HR metric and its acceptance checks, including the vacancy-to-day-90 measure. Show missing links and data coverage separately for Rotterdam, Tilburg, Venlo and flex workers.
lenses.joy: Remove repeated formatting, field copying and document comparisons. Keep the conversations that turn an unclear HR question into a useful, trusted measure.
lenses.options: Generate alternatives for cohort dates, flex-worker inclusion and missing productivity evidence, with worked examples. I choose the definition with HR and the operational owner.
lenses.altitude: I maintain the metric dictionary, specification templates and validation rules. Each report then produces its own draft documentation from those standards.
reach: HR Administrator: define checks for missing employee fields and inconsistent effective dates.
Payroll Specialist: document payroll reconciliation rules for specialist approval.
Controller and FP&A Analyst: maintain shared headcount and labour-cost definitions.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst must settle what a metric means and whether its use is appropriate. 'Productive after 90 days' needs an agreed operational definition; a model cannot infer it reliably from employment status or course completion.
tasks.pattern_why: agent_with_gate combines deterministic metadata extraction and validation with an llm_step that drafts explanations from approved requirements. A person approves business meaning, access rules and the final specification; routine extraction and comparisons run without a model.

in_practice.trigger: An approved request enters a SharePoint list, or a scheduled comparison detects a change in an exported reporting model.
steps: Read the approved request, metric dictionary, source schemas and exported Power BI model metadata.
Use deterministic scripts to list fields, relationships, formulas, refresh dependencies and changes.
Draft the specification from a fixed template, citing source objects and marking unknowns explicitly.
Run schema, reconciliation and access checks against approved examples; flag unsupported joins and definitions.
Present the draft, changes and failed checks to the analyst for review.
After approval, publish the versioned specification in SharePoint and record the validation results.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves every specification; the metric owner approves changed business definitions. Payroll or absence rules go to the relevant specialist, and new employee-data uses go through the company's privacy and applicable OR process.
systems: SharePoint document library and request list
Python or SQL scripts in an approved execution environment
Power Automate for orchestration, subject to licensing and connector checks
data_needed: Model metadata, extraction schemas and existing transformation logic
Approved metric definitions, including numerator, denominator and cohort maturity
Synthetic acceptance examples and approved aggregate reconciliation totals
Access matrix, refresh schedule and document ownership
Relevant CAO interpretations approved by HR or payroll
Stable linkage rules for Recruitee, AFAS and Studytube where those links exist
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint library records source versions, generated drafts, check results, approver and publication time; logs exclude employee-level extracts.

evidence.claim: Power BI TMDL exposes semantic model objects as scripts and supports previews of model changes, providing a practical input for documentation and comparisons.
Generating specifications from metadata, approved definitions and checked examples is plausible, but this complete workflow has not been demonstrated at Noordhaven.

The 65% saving estimates recurring analyst effort: about 33.5 of 51.5 annual hours, worth EUR 2,611 in capacity at EUR 78/hour. The 2.5-fold speedup is a separate active-processing estimate; approval delays, setup and maintenance are excluded.

risks: A polished specification can faithfully describe an incorrect formula; acceptance examples must test business meaning as well as implementation.
Nightly AFAS data cannot establish real-time status, and unmatched candidates or agency workers can distort the hire-to-day-90 denominator.

Metadata may reveal sensitive fields; minimise inputs, restrict access and keep medical details out of the drafting service. Dutch guidance limits what employers may process about illness: [Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens](https://autoriteitpersoonsgegevens.nl/themas/werk-en-uitkering/zieke-werknemers/regels-voor-werkgevers-bij-zieke-werknemers).

Changes to employee-data arrangements or monitoring can require OR consent; route applicable changes before implementation. [SER guidance](https://www.ser.nl/nl/thema/medezeggenschap/belangrijke-themas/privacy).

Documentation assistance needs a different assessment from AI used for recruitment or employee evaluation; expanding into those uses requires an EU AI Act review. [European Commission guidance](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai).
research_questions: Can the current Power BI setup export the required metadata, and are upstream AFAS transformations also accessible?
Across ten recent specifications, how much time went to copying technical facts versus resolving business meaning?
Can generated specifications pass independently written acceptance examples without inventing fields, joins or CAO rules?
Is productivity at day 90 recorded consistently, and can eligible hire cohorts be linked across systems without excluding unmatched hires?

tasks.short: Track HR technology changes and recommend improvements to hiring, onboarding and workforce reporting.

today.trigger: A vendor announces a feature, HR encounters a recurring problem, or the HR Director asks what technology deserves attention.
steps: Translate the business problem into research questions for Noordhaven's HR processes.
Read vendor release notes, documentation and relevant Dutch or EU guidance.
Check fit with AFAS, Recruitee, Studytube, Microsoft 365 and agency data.
Compare likely benefit, integration effort, price and employee impact.
Write a brief and discuss whether to ignore, investigate or pilot the option.
systems: Official vendor websites and release notes
drudgery: Checking the same release-note pages repeatedly
Sorting duplicate announcements and sales claims
Rebuilding the same integration and licensing questions
today.time_sinks: Separating available features from promises and finding out whether Noordhaven's edition, contracts and data can support them. Here the O*NET statement translates to HR service improvement rather than product sales.

lenses.faster: Collect and deduplicate approved sources automatically, then draft a comparison against our systems and HR priorities. I spend time checking decisive claims and assessing fit.
lenses.autonomous: A newly detected release or guidance change starts an evidence brief. The workflow holds unverified pricing, availability and integration claims for review.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain a current view of changes affecting all four HR value streams. Test promising improvements against productive hires retained at day 90, with results split by site and employment group.
lenses.joy: Remove repeated browsing and vendor-summary copying. Keep the investigation, conversations with warehouse managers and decisions about which problem deserves a pilot.
lenses.options: Compare five routes where useful: configure existing software, improve the process, build a small integration, buy a tool or defer. Include ongoing cost and data readiness for each.
lenses.altitude: I design the research criteria and pilot scorecards. The system supplies evidence, while I manage a small portfolio of measurable HR improvements.
reach: HR Director: prepare the evidence and pilot results behind the HR technology roadmap.
Recruiter and L&D Specialist: investigate changes to hiring and certificate workflows.
Controller and FP&A Analyst: prepare technology cost and benefit scenarios for review.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst understands whether a feature solves a real problem on Noordhaven's shifts and sites. Vendor claims cannot establish employee acceptance, CAO fit, manager adoption or a causal improvement in 90-day outcomes.
tasks.pattern_why: agent_with_gate gathers several sources and prepares a recommendation for approval. Deterministic software schedules checks and removes duplicates; an llm_step extracts claims with citations. Strategic prioritisation remains human even if most of the research pack is automated.

in_practice.trigger: A scheduled source check detects new material, or HR submits a technology question through an approved request list.
steps: Retrieve permitted public release notes, official documentation and regulatory updates from an approved source list.
Record dates and source versions, remove duplicates and identify material changes.
Extract claims into a fixed table with citations, availability status and unanswered questions.
Compare options against the system inventory, HR problem backlog, budget assumptions and privacy requirements.
Draft a recommendation and pilot scorecard, separating sourced facts from estimates.
Let the analyst verify decisive claims and approve a brief for the HR Director.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves each recommendation; the HR Director approves spending or a pilot. IT and the privacy lead assess integrations and employee-data use, with the OR involved where applicable.
systems: SharePoint source register and research library
Approved retrieval scripts and enterprise LLM service, proposed
Power BI for approved pilot outcome reporting
data_needed: Current product editions, licences, contract terms and supported integrations
Approved technology source list and dated source documents
HR problem backlog and baseline process volumes
Aggregate time-to-hire, offer acceptance, onboarding and mature 90-day cohort outcomes
Approved CAO constraints and existing OR agreements
Pilot costs, implementation effort and agreed success measures
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint evidence register stores source links, retrieval dates, extracted claims, uncertainty, analyst decisions and pilot outcomes.

evidence.claim: Power Automate supports scheduled cloud flows, providing the recurring trigger for a source-checking workflow; retrieval and research logic still need configuration or development.
An LLM can plausibly extract and compare claims from retrieved documents, provided each important claim is checked against its source.

The 55% saving estimates recurring analyst effort: about 24.6 of 44.7 annual hours, worth EUR 1,918 in capacity at EUR 78/hour. The twofold speedup estimates active research turnaround; vendor response delays, setup and maintenance are excluded.

risks: A release announcement may describe a preview, optional module or unsupported integration; record availability separately from vendor promises.
Retrieved pages can contain instructions aimed at manipulating the research agent; treat pages as evidence and restrict tool permissions.

Research can drift into automated candidate ranking or worker evaluation. Assess the intended use under the EU AI Act before any pilot; human approval alone does not settle classification. [European Commission guidance](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai).
A proposed tool may change employee-data processing or monitoring and require OR consent. [SER guidance](https://www.ser.nl/nl/thema/medezeggenschap/belangrijke-themas/privacy).
Site, shift and seasonal differences can make a pilot appear successful without improving outcomes; compare mature cohorts and avoid attributing every change to the tool.
With only 44.7 annual hours on this task, an elaborate research platform could cost more than the capacity it releases.
research_questions: Can approved sources be retrieved reliably under their access terms, including Dutch material and version histories?
On twenty sampled claims, does the brief cite evidence that actually supports availability, integration and licensing statements?
Did recent research briefs change a decision, and would more frequent monitoring have changed it earlier?
Does a small pilot improve research quality and save enough time to cover setup, licences and ongoing review?

role.altitude: The analyst becomes the owner of HR measurement definitions, reporting controls and evidence for technology decisions, while automated workflows prepare documentation and research.
reach: Maintain shared headcount and labour-cost definitions with the Controller and FP&A team.
Design employee-data quality checks with HR Administration.
Prepare hiring and onboarding pilot evaluations with Recruiters and L&D.
Provide the HR Director with a sourced technology backlog and measured pilot results.
role.ceiling_note: These two tasks total 96.2 annual hours, about 6% of the role. The proposed savings release roughly 58 hours, worth EUR 4,529 in capacity before costs; they do not establish savings across the remaining role or a cash reduction. Missing productivity data, integration access and human decisions about definitions, privacy, CAO interpretation and employee impact limit further autonomy.
skills_to_grow: SQL and Python for metadata extraction, reconciliation and maintainable checks
Power BI model documentation, access testing and version management
Metric design for mature hire cohorts and operational productivity
Evidence checking and evaluation of generated documents
AVG/GDPR, OR consultation and EU AI Act use-case assessment
Pilot design, cost modelling and clear communication with shift managers
role.ambitious_version: Build a trusted measurement chain from vacancy through onboarding to day 90 across all three sites. Make definitions, missing data and cohort maturity visible, then use controlled pilots to identify which process or technology changes increase the share of roles filled by productive hires who stay.
